title: Rafael Câmara signs with Haas F1 Team for 2027 season
excerpt:
Haas F1 Team has announced that Rafael Câmara will race with the team in Formula 1 in 2027.

The Brazilian driver currently leads the FIA Formula 2 Drivers' Championship with three wins this season along with four further podiums and five pole positions.

Câmara also has previous experience in Formula 1 machinery with Haas, having driven for them at Testing of Previous Cars (TPC) in August, jumping in the cockpit of the VF-25 at Autódromo Internacional do Algarve in Portimao, Portugal.

Câmara said that he was excited about the opportunity and was focused on his preparations for next season.

“I’m very happy to be joining TGR Haas F1 Team as a Formula 1 driver,” he said. “It’s an important step in my career and I want to thank Gene Haas and Ayao Komatsu for the trust they have placed in me.

“I’m also very grateful to the Scuderia Ferrari Driver Academy for their support and for everything they have contributed to my development over the years, as well as to my family for always being there throughout this journey. Now my focus is on preparing myself in the best possible way for this new challenge. There will be a lot to learn, and I’m looking forward to working closely with the team, understanding the car and continuing to develop as a driver.”

Haas Team Principal Ayao Komatsu also added: “I’m really excited to sign such a young, amazing talent like Rafael Câmara. “I don’t need to tell everyone about his achievements in the junior formulas, it’s been very impressive, and in his rookie season in Formula 2, the speed he’s shown in some very difficult moments, like qualifying in Monaco and Montreal – that all goes to show the potential Rafa has.

“He showed when we had him drive in our TPC program in Portugal that he could handle himself very well with not a huge amount of time to learn the car, he showed us more than just raw speed. Rafa managed to create an environment to get the best out of himself, it was very impressive and certainly the laps he completed were special. We’re all excited about this opportunity and really committed as TGR Haas F1 Team to nurture this talent and provide a place where he can flourish. We want to create an environment where he’s comfortable and supported, where he can really excel in his capabilities.”

title: Van Amersfoort Racing confirms signing of Rashid Al Dhaheri for 2027 campaign
excerpt:
Rashid Al Dhaheri will step up to FIA Formula 3 in 2027 with Van Amersfoort Racing.

The team confirmed that the Emirati driver will move up to F3 after finishing fourth in this year’s Formula Regional European Championship.

Al Dhaheri’s single-seater career began back in 2023 after multiple karting accolades including WSK Champions Cup and Super Master Series OKJ titles in 2021.

The Mercedes Junior Team driver competed full-time in the Italian F4 series for two seasons along with finishing fourth in the UAE F4 championship in 2024.

In 2025, he moved up to FREC and wound up eighth in the standings in what was his rookie campaign, before returning this year and improving to fourth overall.

Speaking about his step up to F3 with VAR, Al Dhaheri said he was excited to be making the jump and taking on a new challenge.

“I’m very proud to be taking the next step into FIA Formula 3 with Van Amersfoort Racing. It is an important milestone in my journey, but I know the hard work is only beginning. I’m proud to represent the UAE and the wider region at this level, and I’m looking forward to learning, improving and giving everything I have on and off the track. Every step has to be earned, and my focus now is on preparing as strongly as possible for 2027. I’m grateful to everyone who has supported me and helped make this opportunity possible.”

Brad Joyce, Team Principal for Van Amersfoort Racing, added: “We’re looking forward to welcome Rashid to Van Amersfoort Racing. He has had a very strong season in Formula Regional, with three wins and eight podiums, finishing in fourth place in the championship. He has shown his pace throughout the year and has been able to fight at the front of a very competitive field. That gives us a good starting point as he steps up to Formula 3. We’re looking forward to working with him during the post season tests and preparing for his first F3 season together.”

title: Yevan David moves to Van Amersfoort Racing for the 2027 season
excerpt:
Van Amersfoort Racing have announced the signing of Yevan David for the 2027 FIA Formula 3 season.

David returns for a second campaign in F3 after a positive rookie year where he finished 18th in the Drivers’ Championship with 35 points – helped by podium in the Silverstone Sprint Race.

Prior to this season he competed in the 2025 Euroformula Open Championship and he finished second in the Standings with six wins and 14 podiums in total.

The 19-year-old is excited to be back to compete in F3 and to be doing so with VAR.

“Stepping into VAR for the 2027 FIA Formula 3 season feels like the right move at the right time,” said David. “The leadership team has a clear vision, proven experience and a competitive mindset that matches how I want to operate.

“I’m excited to learn from them, contribute to that culture and test myself against the strongest field in junior single-seaters. The challenge is big, but so is the opportunity. I’m ready to work, grow and deliver everything I can throughout the 2027 season”

Van Amersfoort Racing Team Principal Brad Joyce added: “We’re pleased to welcome Yevan to Van Amersfoort Racing. He showed great potential in his first FIA Formula 3 season, with a strong second-place finish in the Silverstone Sprint Race.

“Joining the VAR team will give him a new environment for his second year, and our aim is to turn that experience into great results. We’re looking forward to getting to know him and working with him during the post-season test. This will be a good opportunity to prepare for the 2027 season.”

title: A tribute to his father and an F1 Icon: Fernando Barrichello on his Special Helmet Design
excerpt:
Fernando Barrichello recently spoke about his special tribute helmet to his father Rubens Barrichello

Fernando Barrichello had a new look for the final rounds of the season, as he raced with an eye-catching new helmet.

Blending his own design with his father, Rubens, the Brazilian paid tribute to the multi-time Formula 1 race winner. We caught up with him to talk through it all, including the emotional moment he did the big reveal.

“It's a big dream come true for me to be honest. Obviously watching my dad growing up who had such an iconic design that he had always worn since he was a little kid.

“I always wanted to create a place for myself. But I always knew that at some point I really wanted to honour him and pay respect to everything that he's done. I had been thinking about it for a long time, thinking of how I exactly I wanted to do that.

“His helmet is the way it's supposed to be. You can see that the bottom is his helmet and mine is sort of on top.

Barrichello ran the helmet at the final two rounds of the season in Monza and Madrid

“What I wanted to show is that his helmet has always been on the bottom, and mine is just a layer over everything.

“Obviously, everything that I know and believe in this sport, especially the passion that I have for it, has come from him. So it's an honour to be able to do this but just to show that he's always been under everything.

LN4 Fusion confirm the signing of James Egozi for the 2027 season

Kanato Le returns with Hitech for the 2027 Formula 3 season

“I did a big surprise. He had no idea and he didn't know that this was going to happen, and so when we got together, I showed it to him.

“It was a very emotional one to be honest. I got it on video, so it was really nice. It was really nice to see how surprised he was and just how happy he was. Obviously telling him this was really nice, so it was a special one.

“It's pretty cool in that sense. To be honest, like I said, I've always wanted to do it, but the window never really came about too much.

The Brazilian talked through the right process and why it was the right time to design the helmet

“Arai sent me a new helmet mid-season so we could have a second one here, and it was right around the time where he drove his Ferrari at the Red Bull Ring. I saw it there and everything was sort of aligning for it to happen.

“I felt like that was a really good opportunity, and then it was, to be honest, a good couple of weeks with the people from Infinity.

TRIDENT signs Sebastian Wheldon for 2027 campaign

Woohyun Shin returns with Hitech for 2027 season

“We were thinking and doing a bunch of different designs. We thought of many different things and I wanted it to be as special as possible. So we really thought about every single design possible.

“I'm a bit of a pain, so I do have to apologise to them, but the result came out exactly like I wanted it.

“I've jumped in the car with it for the first time to do radio checks, and there's a little mirror on top of the steering wheel, and I can see myself. It was really special.”

title: LN4 Fusion confirm the signing of James Egozi for the 2027 season
excerpt:
LN4 Fusion have confirmed their first driver signing for the 2027 FIA Formula 3 season, with James Egozi joining the team for the upcoming campaign.

Egozi joins the team after a stellar 2026 season, as he started the year finishing second in the Eurocup-3 Spanish Winter Championship.

The American followed that up by winning this year’s Eurocup-3 title with two rounds to spare, having won eight races and achieved 12 podiums in total.

Egozi will now take the next step in his career by graduating to Formula 3, and he spoke of his delight at getting to join the newly formed team.

"I am truly grateful to the entire Team for giving me the opportunity to join such an exciting project with LN4 Fusion,” said Egozi. “I'm ready to continue my development as a driver, and I am hungrier than ever for the 2027 FIA F3 season."

LN4 Fusion Chief Executive Officer Dan Richards added: "We are really delighted to have James on board. He has always been a very interesting prospect, and he made a remarkable breakthrough this year by dominating the Eurocup-3 championship. His results speak for themselves and we look forward to building on that form as we establish ourselves in the FIA Formula 3 Championship."

title: Kanato Le returns with Hitech for the 2027 Formula 3 season
excerpt:
Hitech have confirmed the signing of Kanato Le for the 2027 FIA Formula 3 season, completing their line-up for next season.

Le returns for a second season in F3 after a finishing 20th in the Drivers’ Standings with 30 points – helped by a podium finish in the Budapest Sprint.

The Japanese driver and Hitech have a history together having firstly competed in a full season together in 2023, and Le finished seventh in the British F4 Championship with two wins.

They reunited earlier this year in the Formula Regional Oceania Trophy, and Le ended up sixth in the Standings with one victory and six podiums in total.

This announcement means the British team’s driver lineup for the upcoming campaign is complete following the announcements of Keanu Al Ahzari and Woohyun Shin.

Le and Hitech will now compete together in Formula 3 in 2027, and at the announcement, he expressed how happy he was to be racing with the team.

“I am really looking forward to racing with Hitech in FIA Formula 3 for the 2027 season,” said Le. “It’s a team I know very well after racing with them in British F4 and CTFROC, and I am excited to be part of the team again.

“I am confident that we will have a strong season together. I would also like to thank everyone for the continued support.”

Hitech Team Manager Paul Bellringer also added: “We’re delighted to welcome Kanato back to Hitech and complete our FIA Formula 3 line-up for 2027.

“Kanato is a driver we know very well, having worked with him at different stages of his career. He’s always had good natural speed and racecraft, and it’s been rewarding to see him gain experience and develop over the last few seasons.

“His first year in FIA Formula 3 has given him a much better understanding of the demands of the championship, and he showed what he is capable of with his podium in Hungary and strong qualifying performance at Monza.

“It was also great to have him back racing with us at Brands Hatch recently. He settled straight back in and delivered another podium, which says a lot about his ability to adapt and get up to speed.

“With Kanato confirmed, our 2027 driver line-up is now complete. We have a good combination of talent and experience, and we're looking forward to getting to work with all three drivers as we prepare for next season.”

title: TRIDENT signs Sebastian Wheldon for 2027 campaign
excerpt:
Sebastian Wheldon will step up to FIA Formula 3 in 2027 with TRIDENT.

The Italian team confirmed that the American will race with the Milanese outfit next season after finishing this year’s Formula Regional European Championship campaign in second.

Prior to that, Wheldon debuted in single-seater racing back in 2023, winning the Skip Barber Formula Race Series with six wins.

He moved onto the YACademy Winter Series in 2024, finishing second before finishing the USF Juniors series third overall.

In 2025, he secured seven wins across the F4 Middle East, E4 and Italian F4 Championships, finishing third overall in the latter with six victories, three poles and nine podiums overall.

Speaking about his signing with TRIDENT in F3, Wheldon says that he was excited about the next step in his career.

“I'm very happy to be competing in the 2027 FIA Formula 3 Championship with TRIDENT Motorsport. There's a lot of pressure, as I'll be racing for one of the most successful teams in the category. However, I love a challenge and will give my all to learn quickly and achieve good results. I'm extremely grateful to TWG Motorsports and Andretti Global for their support. I can't wait for next season to begin. Let's go!”

TRIDENT Team Manager Giacomo Ricci added: “We are delighted to announce our agreement with Sebastian Wheldon for the 2027 FIA Formula 3 Championship season. Sebastian is a driver who has demonstrated consistent growth throughout his career, distinguishing himself both in the United States and Europe. His 2026 Formula Regional season, which he finished in second place, confirmed his talent and ability to compete at the highest level. We are confident that Trident Motorsport represents the ideal environment to support him in the next step of his promising career.”

title: Woohyun Shin returns with Hitech for 2027 season
excerpt:
Hitech has confirmed that Woohyun Shin will race with the team in 2027. The South Korean driver competed with the British outfit in 2026 and will return for what will be his second full season in FIA Formula 3.

Prior to F3, Shin secured P3 in the Euroformula Open Championship in 2025, improving on the fifth place he earned in the series the year prior.

He also finished fourth in the 2024 Formula Regional Oceania Championship.

Speaking about his re-signing with Hitech, Shin said he was happy to be back with the team once again.

“There are particular aspects to the FIA Formula 3 championship that make it very competitive and challenging. I felt that there would be more to come from me by staying another year and further working on those areas in a familiar environment.

“I want to thank the team for believing in me and making it possible to continue our journey together.”

Hitech F3 Team Manager Paul Bellringer added: “We’re pleased to continue our relationship with Michael into the 2027 FIA Formula 3 season. This year has been an important learning process for him, returning to FIA F3 for a full campaign after his previous experience in the championship.

“Michael has had to learn a lot throughout the season, from the car and tyres to the level of competition and the demands of racing at this level. Having that experience behind him will be valuable heading into his second year.

“We know Michael well from his previous time with Hitech, and we believe there is a lot more to come from him. Continuity is important in Formula 3, and giving him another season with the team will allow us to build on the work we have already done together.

“We’re looking forward to seeing Michael take the next step in 2027 and continuing his development with Hitech.”

title: Enzo Deligny remains with Van Amersfoort Racing for 2027 season
excerpt:
Van Amersfoort Racing has confirmed that Enzo Deligny will remain with the team for his second FIA Formula 3 campaign in 2027.

Deligny made his debut this year, racing with VAR and finishing the season 16th in the Drivers' Championship, earning a podium on debut in Melbourne.

The Frenchman secured a further two top five finishes and seven top 10 results across the year.

Speaking about his re-signing with Van Amersfoort, Deligny said that he was pleased to be returning with the team.

“I'm really happy to be continuing with VAR for 2027. After joining the team late this season, I immediately felt very comfortable and we’ve built a strong relationship. I’m really looking forward to starting next year together and showing what we can achieve. Having stability by staying with this great team will help me perform next year. I can't wait.”

VAR Team Principal Brad Joyce added: “We’re pleased to continue our collaboration with Enzo for another season. He made a very strong start to his FIA Formula 3 career in Melbourne, finishing second in the Sprint Race on his debut weekend. He has now gained a full year of experience in the championship, and working with him throughout the season has given us the opportunity to see his talent up close. That experience and continuity are important as we look to build on what we started in 2026 and push for stronger results in 2027.”

title: Keanu Al Azhari joins Hitech for 2027 campaign
excerpt:
Hitech has announced that Keanu Al Azhari will step up to FIA Formula 3 with the team next season.

The 18-year-old joins the Championship after competing with Hitech across multiple seasons. In 2025 in GB3, the combination brought a race win, six podiums and three pole positions.

This year, he has raced with Hitech in the Eurocup-3 Spanish Winter Championship and Eurocup-3. In the former, Al Azhari earned two wins and seven podiums to win the title. In Eurocup-3, the Emirati driver currently sits third in the standings with two rounds to go with a race win to his name.

Al Alzhari said that he was proud to be representing the UAE and was very excited about his graduation to F3 with the Hitech team.

“I am proud and honoured to continue my journey with my family at Hitech as we step up together into the 2027 FIA Formula 3 Championship.

“To become the first driver from the UAE to compete in FIA Formula 3 is a milestone I carry with immense pride. Representing my nation at this level is the greatest honour, and I'm humbled by the support of the UAE behind me.

“I hope this journey inspires the next generation of drivers across our region to dream without limits.”

Paul Bellringer, Hitech’s FIA F3 Team Manager added: “It’s great to see Keanu making the step into FIA Formula 3 with us. We’ve worked closely with him over the last two seasons and have seen first-hand how much he has developed in that time.

“He has shown his speed with race wins and podiums, but one of his real strengths is his ability to race his way through the field. Even when a weekend hasn’t gone to plan or conditions are difficult, he finds a way to move forward and put himself in contention. That ability to make something out of challenging situations will serve him well in Formula 3.

“There’s something particularly rewarding about seeing a driver progress through the different levels of Hitech and reach F3 with us. Keanu knows how we work, we know what he is capable of, and we’re looking forward to continuing that progression together in 2027.”

title: FIA Formula 3 unveils 2027 calendar
excerpt:
The FIA Formula 3 Championship has announced its 2027 calendar, featuring 10 rounds across four continents and three exciting new venues: Jeddah, Montreal and Istanbul.

The campaign will bring Formula 3 to North America for the first time, while expanding further the Championship’s international footprint.

The season will begin in March with two back-to-back events. Sakhir, Bahrain, will host the opening round alongside Formula 1 and Formula 2 before the field travels to Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, where the 30 F3 cars will take on the fast and demanding Jeddah Corniche Circuit for the very first time.

Melbourne, Australia, will follow in April, before Formula 3 makes its historic North American debut in May. Montreal will host Round 4, offering the drivers another new challenge at the Circuit Gilles-Villeneuve.

The Championship will return to the streets of Monaco, in June for two back-to-back rounds will then take place in July, beginning at Silverstone, Great Britain, and followed by Spielberg, Austria.

After the summer break, the season will resume with another double-header. The teams and drivers will first compete at Monza, Italy, before travelling to Madrid, Spain.

Finally, the 2027 campaign will conclude at Istanbul, Türkiye, the third new venue on the calendar. Formula 3’s first visit to Istanbul Park will provide a demanding and fitting finale to a season of unprecedented geographical reach.

Mohammed Ben Sulayem, FIA President said: ““Formula 3 is where many drivers begin to prove themselves on the international stage, and the 2027 calendar will give them an exceptional range of challenges where they can develop their skills. Racing in North America for the first time is an important milestone for the Championship, while the additions of Jeddah and Istanbul will test our drivers across demanding circuits.

“Providing young talent with these experiences is fundamental to building the future of our sport, and I look forward to watching this next generation rise to the challenge throughout the 2027 season.”

Stefano Domenicali, President and CEO of Formula 1 said: "We have seen great racing in Formula 3 in 2026, including an incredible fight for the title, which ultimately went to the first ever American driver to win the Championship, and the 2027 season is set to build on that momentum with another exciting generation of young talent coming through the motorsport pyramid. Racing alongside Formula 1 is a unique opportunity for these drivers to develop their skills, showcase their potential and prepare themselves for the demands of the highest level of our sport. The 2027 calendar marks an exciting step for Formula 3, with the Championship visiting four continents and introducing new venues that will provide fresh challenges for drivers and teams alike. I would like to thank the FIA President and their entire team, Bruno Michel and his team, as well as our promoters, partners, officials, marshals and volunteers, whose dedication and commitment make the Championship possible. Formula 3 continues to play a vital role in developing the stars of tomorrow, and I look forward to another outstanding season of racing in 2027."

Bruno Michel, FIA Formula 3 CEO said: “The 2027 FIA Formula 3 calendar is groundbreaking, with three new venues that represent a formidable challenge for the teams and the drivers. It will be very exciting to see the F3 cars at the Jeddah Corniche Circuit, and I’m extremely pleased to bring F3 to North America for the very first time thanks to the addition of Montreal to the calendar. Istanbul Park will host the season finale, another new challenge next season. Just like for F2, we will be covering freight costs so that the territorial expansion of the calendar does not financially impact our teams.”

title: Maciej Gladysz Season Review: Maiden win and important lessons learned
excerpt:
Maciej Gladysz enjoyed a decent rookie season in FIA Formula 3, with a maiden Feature Race victory at Silverstone the highlight of 2026 for the ART Grand Prix driver.

The Polish driver was able to secure 12th in the Drivers' Standings with multiple top 10 finishes and that victory the peak of the season.

"I'm not too happy with the season overall. I think there were many rounds that I messed up. I think Monaco or Barcelona should have gone much better. Or even Hungary, where I started from P2 and I had one of the worst starts of the year.

"Then Monza, I was not too quick and I had a big problem with the car as well. So overall, the season's not gone the way I would have wanted."

Though he feels the season didn't pan out in the manner he'd hoped for ahead of the campaign, it was down to a lack of consistency rather than any missing speed according to the Polish driver.

"I think the consistency's been missing this year. I think when everything was going well with myself and with the car, I think we were always up there.

"We've just struggled a bit for rhythm this season. It's obviously nice to see my teammates scoring points. I mean, in Monza it was really helpful because we went from 5th to 3rd in one round, so it was good, but obviously it's not too nice to see.

"It's nice to see my teammates winning, but it's not nice when you're not fighting with them for the top steps.

"So, I was happy for them but disappointed at the same time because obviously you want to be the top teammate. But that is one of the big lessons this year I think: being humble.

"You can't be too confident. I mean, once you have a good weekend you need to approach with the same confidence and with the same approach you had the weekend before.

"Some drivers will improve, you get frustrated with your result but if you get one bad result and you can't just give up. You just need to bounce back straight away and work as hard as you can. Every weekend is a big weekend."

Though the second half of his campaign didn't reach the same heights as he'd hoped, Gladysz says he was happy to have secured a win in his rookie campaign.

He also learned that resilience was vital, and that is a big factor he'll be carrying into the future of his career.

"Silverstone, it's been the best one. In the Sprint Race, things went well, we finished in 6th position and then we had the Feature Race.

"We started from eighth, finished in fourth and then after post-race penalties we managed to take a win. So yeah, it was the best weekend because the previous three weekends I was almost not even in the points.

"That weekend I scored 30 points and went from 16th position in the championship to sixth, just being 15 points away from P3. So that was probably the highlights of the year."

title: Pedro Clerot Season Review: Patience, adaptation and victory
excerpt:
It took until the final round of the season, but Pedro Clerot made sure his obvious speed counted for a victory in FIA Formula 3 2026.

The Rodin Motorsport driver claimed the Madrid Feature Race 1 win, an emotional milestone and one he was fully deserving of after an impressive campaign as a rookie.

His five podium finishes helped him to sixth in the Championship, level on points with Théophile Nael in fifth and behind only on countback.

Reflecting on his efforts across the season, Clerot said that he was happy to have achieved the important results in a tricky year, capped off with his finest round in the Championship to date.

"I think up and down," he surmised. "For sure it was not maybe the year that we deserve and maybe wanted, with some things out of our control, some others went off, but overall I'm proud with the team.

"We achieved five podiums, including a win, which is quite remarkable. We got the first one in Monaco, then a very good round in Spielberg with almost a double podium, really good, really strong weekend and to top it off Spa, which is a special track.

Clerot secured his maiden F3 win at the final round of the season in Madrid

"(Madrid) was a really special, really special weekend. It is really good to finally show what we had I'd say the whole year in terms of pace.

"It's unfortunate that Monza didn't go away, I think we were set to fight for at least another podium."

Clerot says that he and the Rodin team were able to build momentum in the middle of the season despite a tough run of results. Podiums in Monte Carlo, Spielberg and Spa gave way to a run of six races out of the points.

He believes rebounding in Madrid was proof of his learnings as a rookie, with the team showing a decent ability to bounce back from tougher results.

"I focus on what I can control and what I've done. We had a lot of moments in the season that were out of our control. Monza for example where two really strong results got thrown in the bin for situations that we cannot control, one a technical issue and the second a crash.

FIA Formula 3 announces 2026 post-season tests in Jerez and Barcelona

"In the end I think it's about maximising the things I can control and what we can control as a team. I think we've been up there, we showed that we can for sure fight, we come back even when we sometimes start a bit further away from points. I'm proud of what the team has achieved."

Overall, Clerot points to the team's impressive pace as their main strength across the 2026 campaign. His ability to move forward in races after tougher Qualifying outcomes was evidence of this, adding that better results could have been on the cards had Fridays gone more smoothly.

"Race pace in general has been really strong. We've come back to the field multiple times starting outside the top 20 to score some points.

"I think the team have given me a lot of help to understand degradation and what we can do in the races to actually make a difference and I think it stands out.

Overall the Brazilian was happy with his efforts in 2026 and will be back next season with Rodin

"Red Bull Ring, two races that we showed that we were one of the quickest, if not the quickest on track, pace has never been an issue.

"I think it's difficult to say that the pace was not there on a single lap either because I think we had the pace to be inside the top 12 every qualifying, it's just sometimes being a bit unlucky with things out of our control, put us out of that top 12.

"For sure there's work to be done everywhere, things that maybe we could have done better as a driver and also maybe as a team but anyway, I'm proud of what we achieved."

Reflecting on his rookie season and after having been confirmed to return with Rodin in 2027, Clerot will be carrying vital experience with him into next year.

Picking out the most important aspects however, he looks at how the team were able to remain calm despite results not arriving as expected and the ability to refocus quickly as vital elements he'll take into '27.

"Patience and resetting. During the race weekend, everything happens so quick. The season happens so fast with the summer races that you just have to reset after every race and come back with a fresh mindset, focus on each weekend and not the big picture.

"That is what we learn in this championship – adapting. You do 2-3 laps in FP, 2-3 push in Quali and then that's it. That's your weekend set. Sometimes you can turn things around and sometimes push those results even better but sometimes not."

title: FIA Formula 3 announces 2026 post-season tests in Jerez and Barcelona
excerpt:
The FIA Formula 3 Championship can confirm that there will be two post-season tests across Jerez and Barcelona to complete the 2026 season.

Both tests will be two-day events, with the first test being held at the Circuito de Jerez from October 20-21.

The teams and drivers will then make the trip to the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya for the final two days of on-track action in 2026 on October 26-27.

Fans will be able to follow the action on the FIA Formula 3 website, with live blogs keeping you up to date with the action, as well as session reports and interviews at the end of each day.

Stay tuned to all our social media channels throughout the day for the behind the scenes viewing of each day of post-season testing, as the teams begin their preparations for the 2027 campaign.

title: Noah Stromsted Season Review: Improvements and opportunities
excerpt:
Noah Stromsted returned in 2026 with TRIDENT for a second campaign in FIA Formula 3. The Dane was aiming to fight for the title this time around, and secured victories and podiums but ultimately fell short.

Reflecting on his campaign, the TRIDENT driver says there were plenty of ups and downs but that he felt he made improvements across the board from his rookie season in 2025.

"I think the start of the season there were ups and downs," he said. "In the second half of the season there have been quite a few things out of our control which has affected our season quite a lot. So I've not had the results I had been hoping for this season.

"I've definitely made steps forward. There's been steps forward in everything in my driving. Unfortunately, it's not shown in the results because of some issues we've had this year.

"When we've had good days - we've had a really good pace. In Austria, we had a good qualifying, and then mega pace in both the Sprint and the Feature Race. On our good days, we've been really quick."

Stromsted admitted that his season hadn't gone as smoothly as he might have liked, highlighting errors and events that were both in and out of his and the team's control.

However, he also believes that he was able to improve across many different areas, with race management being a big strength of his throughout 2026.

"Some of the races have been, from my side, weren't always the best. Australia - I was looking to finish P3 in the Feature Race and got a penalty. In Monaco I also got a penalty for both races. So, for sure, some of it has been my fault, being a bit too aggressive at the start.

"The rest has been outside of our control. I think it was quite clear from last year was I had work to do in terms of qualifying, also a bit at the start of this season.

"But I think, as the season progressed, it has been quite good, just not showing up results-wise, but driving-wise it's been quite good. I also think in the races, a bit like in 2025, what has always just clicked for me in the races is tyre management and when to push and when to take it easy."

Rodin Motorsport confirms Reza Seewooruthun for 2027 F3 season

Hiyu Yamakoshi Season Review: 'A positive surprise' after multiple podiums in 2026

Overall, it's no surprise that the victory around the Red Bull Ring stands out as his moment of the year.

In a race where rivals peaked and then fell away, Stromsted was able to demonstrate his racecraft and management to rise above the rest.

"Austria Feature Race - the pace that we came was really strong from the start to finish. With the crash in the Sprint Race compromised the result a bit there. Otherwise, I think a double podium would have been also very likely."

title: Rodin Motorsport confirms Reza Seewooruthun for 2027 F3 season
excerpt:
Reza Seewooruthun will step up to FIA Formula 3 with Rodin Motorsport in 2027 the team has confirmed.

The 20-year-old steps up with the team having raced with them in the 2026 Formula Regional European Championship, so far earning two podiums across the campaign.

The Briton graduated from karts in 2022, and made a full-time debut in the Ginnetta Junior Championship the following year.

In 2024, he finishing fourth in the British F4 Championship, and also competed in the UAE F4 and Euro 4 Championships. He then moved to GB3 in 2025 where he finished fifth in the standings that season.

Speaking about his step up to FIA F3, Seewooruthun said that he was honoured to be racing with Rodin once again.

“I’m proud to be staying with Rodin Motorsport as I move into Formula 3 next year. It’s an honour to make that step with a team I trust. I’m excited for this next chapter, but the next few months are focused on hard work before we get to the season opener.”

Rodin Sporting Director Benn Huntingford added: “It’s great to see Reza continuing his development with the team as he steps up to FIA Formula 3. He’s shown some promising pace throughout his time in FREC and secured two podiums this season, which have been important milestones in his progression. We’re looking forward to building on that experience with him and seeing what he can achieve in F3.”

title: Brando Badoer's Season Review: Highlight moments and bouncing back from tough rookie year
excerpt:
Brando Badoer is delighted with how well he bounced back from his rookie season to put in a stronger campaign with Rodin Motorsport in 2026.

The Italian driver ended the year seventh in the Championship after a 2025 campaign where he finished 25th in the Standings.

Speaking at the finale in Madrid, Badoer spoke with the pride at the season he has put together this year.

“It's definitely been a good season overall,” he said. “Lots of good races, important races and memories with the team. Of course, we got the Monaco win, and we got four podiums, and we worked really well throughout the year.

“Coming into the last round we were a couple of points off P3 in the championship, in the top five. It was a really good fight for it so definitely a strong season overall.

“I think overall we had a lot of positive things. Some things we could have done better. Every year when you look back at the season, there are a lot of things where you think I lost points there or there. But it's normal and it's that way for everyone.

Badoer finished eighth in the Standings after ending up 25th in 2025

“Sometimes we got good luck, sometimes bad luck. But overall I can be happy about the work I've done in F3, and I'm really thankful for every part of the team, the mechanics, engineers, the team manager, for all the work they've done alongside me.”

When asked what he felt he had improved upon this year compared to 2025, Badoer responded: “I'm definitely happy to have shown the world my potential. The worst season was last year.

“I usually always perform at a high level, but last year for many reasons it was impossible. Definitely tough moments make you stronger.

Ernesto Rivera Season Review: Mental resilience, pure speed and more to come

IMAGE GALLERY: A look through Freddie Slater's 2026 season in pictures

“I think I still managed to comeback very strong and motivated for 2026, and with the help of a team that for me has been like a family, in Rodin. It was possible to fight at the top of the Standings.

“So I would say the determination, motivation and the support of my team made it possible. People forget about a negative 2025, which was definitely a tough one to deal with.”

Badoer concedes that consistency was something he improved on this year even if it was not always perfect, as he acknowledged that Formula 3 is a “difficult championship to be always competitive in”.

Badoer praised Rodin for their work with him this season

But that didn’t change the 20-year-old’s approach, who believes his hard work was the biggest strength this season.

“Maybe it might sound a bit obvious, but I would say the hard work,” said Badoer when asked about his biggest strength in 2026. “Going into every tiny detail when things are not as good as they should.

Pedro Clerot returns with Rodin Motorsport for the 2027 season

IMAGE GALLERY: Some of the best pictures from the final round in Madrid

“It helps you fix them and make them good for the next time. So I would say the really hard and deep work always gets you out of tough situations. So I would say that's the key.”

When asked to pick a highlight moment, Badoer said: “Winning in Monaco. I've had many good moments, but for sure that stands out.

“I think I achieved it, and it was a good celebration. It was a good celebration, but not long because I had Barcelona.”

title: Ernesto Rivera Season Review: Mental resilience, pure speed and more to come
excerpt:
While it was hardly the start Ernesto Rivera would have been hoping for in 2026, seventh in his rookie FIA Formula 3 campaign capped off a positive year for the Mexican driver.

Driving for Campos Racing and helping the Spanish outfit to a second consecutive Teams' Championship and was vying for a top three finish in the Drivers' Standings in his own right.

A difficult final round in Madrid proved costly, but that hardly detracts from what was a very impressive debut in the Championship.

His season started on the worst note possible as injury ahead of pre-season testing left him facing an uphill struggle and behind his rivals in terms of preparation.

"I think it has gone really well, for sure better than what I expected and probably what most people expected," Rivera explained.

"I missed the start the season because of the back injury and also missed the pre-season test. But since Monaco I've been on it honestly. For sure I've made some mistakes and lost some points but I think it's been a really good rookie campaign."

Going into depth on the struggles he endured in the early months of the season, Rivera explained that it was a challenge mentally as well as physically.

"I was having a tough campaign in New Zealand, in the Formula Regional Oceania, and yeah honestly I just wanted to get back to Europe and start with the test in F3 and with Campos.

Rivera started 2026 on the back foot but quickly made up for lost time

"It was tough having the injury in the last race of the championship in New Zealand. I ended up having to go to Mexico, and in that first week, I was only able to walk, not do anything else and I was just sitting there watching the times of the test and yeah, it was tough mentally the first week.

"After that I just said to myself there's nothing you can do, just try to treat the recovery as positively as possible and let's see if you can come back to Melbourne.

"We decided I couldn't race in Melbourne because I was not even going to the gym yet, I still had a lot of pain.

"I lost a lot of muscle. I was like six kilos lighter because of the muscle loss, so it was tough to be as prepared as possible for Monaco."

TRIDENT confirm the signing of Kean Nakamura-Berta for the 2027 season

Pedro Clerot returns with Rodin Motorsport for the 2027 season

When he did get in the F3 car, he delivered instantly. P5 on Feature Race debut around the streets of Monte Carlo underlined his potential, and the 2026 season only grew from there for Rivera.

Three races later, he was standing on the top step of an F3 podium for the first time, victor of the Spielberg Sprint Race and the strong start caught the Campos driver by surprise also.

"I thought I could do good, not as good as I've done honestly. I didn't have such high expectations, but yeah I think I made a lot of progress. I've tried to work really hard and improve in all the areas as possible.

The Red Bull Junior Team Driver says he was proud to achieve multiple wins with Campos this year

"Qualifying, I've always been there, but maybe the races I've struggled a bit more with tyre deg and I've been improving quite a lot. I hope to carry these learnings for the rest of my career."

After the Sprint win, the next target was a Feature Race victory, and he didn't have to wait long. It arrived around the circuit he rates as his favourite on the calendar, and it was arguably his most complete drive in the Championship.

Rivera says it was a showcase of his learnings across the season, from tyre and race management to wheel-to-wheel battling and working with his team.

"For sure winning in Spa is my highlight. It's my favourite track of Europe and I did a great race. The car was great, tyre management was great and yeah, overall it was a good weekend. It's where I gained a lot of points, climbed the standings with that win and I think that is the highlight of the season."

After a challenging campaign, with setbacks, peaks and highlight moments, Rivera says that there are plenty of takeaways from the 2026 campaign. The biggest point however is self-belief.

"I've got to trust myself more. Sometimes last year I wasn't so confident in myself and after this year, I know that I can do it.

"I think it has helped me a lot, for my confidence, I think that's where I improved a lot away from the driving side of things. I started to trust myself more and handle those pressure scenarios better."

title: Pedro Clerot returns with Rodin Motorsport for the 2027 season
excerpt:
Rodin Motorsport has confirmed that Pedro Clerot will continue with the team for a second season in FIA Formula 3 in 2027.

Clerot had a strong rookie campaign with Rodin, finishing sixth in the Drivers' Championship helped by his five podiums – which include a Feature Race 1 victory at the final round in Madrid.

Prior to that, the 19-year-old won the 2022 Brazilian F4 title and finished fourth in the 2025 Formula Regional European Championship.

Clerot is now set to return for a second season in Formula 3, and the Brazilian driver expressed his delight at being able to do so in an environment where he feels very comfortable.

“I’m very happy to be staying with Rodin for my second year in FIA F3,” said Clerot. “We’ve built a really strong relationship this season and achieved some great results, improving race after race. I’ve felt at home with the team since day one, so continuing this journey together is very special.

“I believe we have what it takes to fight at the front next season, and I’m excited to see what we can achieve together.”

Rodin Motorsport Sporting Director Benn Huntingford added: “We’re delighted to continue our relationship with Pedro for another season in FIA Formula 3. He’s really impressed the team this year, showing strong pace and making great progress throughout the season. To see him take his maiden win in Madrid was a fantastic way to end the year and a result that reflects the progress he’s made. We’re looking forward to building on that next season and seeing what we can achieve together.”

title: TRIDENT confirm the signing of Kean Nakamura-Berta for the 2027 season
excerpt:
TRIDENT have announced the signing of Kean Nakamura-Berta for the 2027 FIA Formula 3 campaign – the first confirmed driver for the upcoming season.

Having made the step up from karting in 2023, Nakamura-Berta boasts an impressive record in single seaters having won 2025 Italian F4 and E4 Championships titles.

In 2026, the Williams Driver Academy member won Formula Regional Middle East Trophy title, and he also finished third in the Formula Regional European Championship.

Nakamura-Berta is now set to graduate to Formula 3 in 2027, and at the announcement, he expressed his delight at the opportunity to race with TRIDENT.

“I’m pleased to be stepping up to F3 with TRIDENT Motorsport while still having the ongoing support of the Williams F1 Team Driver Academy,” said Nakamura-Berta.

“Finishing the season strongly in FREC and having the opportunity to join such a competitive team in F3 gives me great confidence as I look ahead to my F3 debut next year. A big thank you to everyone involved who helped get me here.”

TRIDENT Team Manager Giacomo Ricci added: “We are extremely pleased to announce the arrival of Kean Nakamura-Berta at TRIDENT Motorsport for the 2027 FIA Formula 3 Championship season. Kean is a driver we have known and followed for some time, and he has demonstrated he has all the qualities needed to take this important step. His journey, from karting to Formula Regional, has been marked by constant growth and impressive results. It will be a pleasure to begin this collaboration and work together to best prepare for such an important campaign. We are convinced that Trident represents the ideal environment to allow Kean to continue his growth and express his full potential in the FIA Formula 3 series.”

Williams F1 Team Sporting Director Sven Smeets also added: “It's a proud moment to see Kean step up to F3 with Trident Motorsport for his rookie season. He has made impressive progress since joining the Academy this year, and this opportunity is a culmination of the hard work and dedication he's shown across a long and hard-fought title campaign, backed by an already outstanding record. This is a great moment for the Driver Academy, and a fitting reflection of the opportunities it creates for the next generation of talented drivers.”

title: Clerot reflects on ‘really special’ Madrid weekend after claiming maiden victory
excerpt:
Pedro Clerot was pleased to bring a very “successful season” to a close with a special performance in Madrid – the Brazilian claiming his maiden Formula 3 victory in Feature Race 1.

The Rodin Motorsport driver was impressive at the Madring circuit, missing out on pole position by 0.012s in Qualifying 1 on Friday.

Clerot was then in the fight for pole on his final lap in Qualifying 2 but hit the barrier at the last corner and settled for third place.

The Brazilian driver then made a great start from P2 in Feature Race 1 to take the lead and the victory before adding another podium to his weekend tally with a P3 in Sunday’s race.

Speaking on his way out of the paddock with his two trophies in hand, Clerot reflected on a strong few days in the Spanish capital.

Clerot achieved his maiden win in Formula 3 in dominant style in Feature Race 1

“It was a really special, really special weekend,” he said. “It is really good to finally show what we had, maybe I'd say the whole year in terms of pace.

“Obviously, I'm not going to say luck was on our side, we did the work, we put a lot there in qualifying and we had a very good start yesterday.

Taponen reflects on ‘satisfying’ end to the season after victory in Madrid

‘We’ve been incredible all season’ says Slater as he reflects on 2026 campaign and title loss

“We controlled the race, had really good pace, and the car was incredible. The team did an amazing job, obviously driving was on point as well this weekend, so I’m really happy to put a very strong weekend to end the year.”

Speaking more about Feature Race 2, Clerot spoke about his mindset when out on track, admitted a move on Ugo Ugochukwu was never really on, but not for a lack of effort on his part.

“It's very difficult to overtake around here,” he said. “Obviously I was thinking more about the points as well. We're fighting for the team's championship as well, so just took it a little bit more careful today.

Clerot made sure to keep it clean out on track to achieve the best results

“But I didn't really have the opportunity to try to go for the overtake with Ugo. I know he was risking a bit more than me by fighting the championship.

“But anyway it’s another podium, another 15 points in the bag, we showed really good pace on such a difficult track like this, and to be this competitive is very nice, so I'm very happy.”

TITLE-WINNING ANALYSIS: The moment that earned Ugochukwu the 2026 title

IMAGE GALLERY: All the best photos from Ugo Ugochukwu's title-winning weekend in Madrid

Clerot’s strong weekend saw him end the season sixth in the Drivers' Championship, and while he is happy with the result, he does not feel it properly represents his and Rodin’s performance levels.

“P6 in the championship maybe doesn't reflect what I think we had,” said the Brazilian. “Nut anyway, five podiums this year is very special.

“It's a very successful rookie season, some coulda, woulda, shouldas out there, but I’m just very happy to end the season like this.”

title: Taponen reflects on ‘satisfying’ end to the season after victory in Madrid
excerpt:
Tuukka Taponen claimed his maiden FIA Formula 3 victory in the Madrid Feature Race 2 – and that earned him third place in the Drivers’ Championship.

The MP Motorsport driver had a great final round, finishing third in Qualifying 1 and taking pole position in Qualifying 2.

Taponen would convert that into a podium in Feature Race 1 and held off champion Ugo Ugochukwu in Feature Race 2 to take the victory.

Speaking at the end of the weekend, the Finnish driver says staying ahead of his Campos Racing rival was vital to the victory.

“It was a good start,” said Taponen. “I thought about it last night that I really want to focus on the start. I wanted to make sure I was ready.

Taponen was impressive in Madrid converting pole into victory

“Everyone starting on the grid knew that was crucial because overtaking is difficult later on. It was a good start, and after that, I controlled and managed the race. I picked up the pace when needed. In the end, I built up a gap to Ugo.

“Overtaking is hard, so I wasn't too worried. I focused on sector one and sector two, then shifted focus slightly to sector three to build a gap for sector one.

‘We’ve been incredible all season’ says Slater as he reflects on 2026 campaign and title loss

TITLE-WINNING ANALYSIS: The moment that earned Ugochukwu the 2026 title

“Turn 5 is the main overtaking opportunity which is very tricky. I made sure not to make any major mistakes. Eventually, I opened up enough of a gap, so I wasn't worried.”

“But it’s a great achievement. Of course, not every Finn has reached this point, so I’m happy to have won.”

Taponen finished third in the Drivers' Championship after a strong end to the season

title: ‘We’ve been incredible all season’ says Slater as he reflects on 2026 campaign and title loss
excerpt:
Freddie Slater admitted he was gutted to have not fought for the title in the way he wanted in Madrid. But he also paid tribute to rival Ugo Ugochukwu, Campos Racing and his team TRIDENT.

The British driver went into the weekend with a 15-point lead over Ugochukwu in the Standings, but was 17th in Qualifying 1 and eighth in Qualifying 2 after dealing with an issue on his car.

Ugochukwu, on the other hand, was fourth and second, and on a track where it is tough to overtake, Slater could not do much to catch up with his rival in all three races.

Both drivers were tied going into Sunday’s final Feature Race, and with Ugochukwu second and Slater seventh, the American took the title.

Reflecting on it all afterwards, Slater said: “Obviously a little bit gutted with the end result, but fundamentally we had too many things go wrong. The Feature Race in Monza, that was the start of it, and then this weekend in qualifying we had too many issues.

“On a track like this it's very difficult to overtake as well, so when you're at the back or in the mid-pack it's always going to be difficult. To be fair, fair play to Ugo and Campos, they had a good weekend.

Slater struggled in Qualfying in Madrid as he and TRIDENT struggled with an issue

“But we didn't really get the fight we wanted with the issues we had but overall it doesn't detract from the season we've had.

“We've done an amazing job all year to be a rookie with the performances we've had, we’ve been incredible all year. So it's just a shame that sometimes motorsport is like that, but that's how it is sometimes.”

Reflecting on the season as a whole, Slater had one win, three pole positions and eight podiums in total. Despite it not leading to the title, he views the year with a huge amount of positivity.

TITLE-WINNING ANALYSIS: The moment that earned Ugochukwu the 2026 title

IMAGE GALLERY: All the best photos from Ugo Ugochukwu's title-winning weekend in Madrid

“I think as a rookie, trying to gain the experience and get on level with the second-year drivers as quick as I could has been really well managed,” he said.

“The pace has been incredible all year, very consistent, and executed all the time. Unfortunately there's some variables that went the wrong way out of our control, and those affect the results.

“They came at the worst possible time if I'm honest, because obviously there's no time now to catch up, it's over. So a little bit gutted the way we couldn't really finish the job off and really fight for it and show what we have been all season.

Slater's 2027 plans are already set as he will race in Formula 2 with Invicta Racing

“But it doesn't take away what we've done all year. We've done an amazing job, and I couldn't have done that without my team, TRIDENT. So a massive thank you to them.”

Slater’s 2027 plans have already been announced as he will step up to FIA Formula 2 with Invicta Racing. His goal now is to make sure he is ready for the challenges that lie ahead.

“We’ve still been fighting for another championship,” he continued. "It's another year done and another championship nearly won. So it's been an impressive career so far.

“But now there's some exciting things hopefully to come in the future. Still a steep hill to climb, that's for sure. So I need to continue to keep pushing and try and develop into a better driver, that's the aim of the game.

“So we're going to have a nice off-season, mostly with friends and family, and relax a little bit. But also get ready for next year to see what that holds.”

title: ‘This was my main goal’ says Ugochukwu after sealing Formula 3 title in Madrid
excerpt:
Ugo Ugochukwu is the 2026 Drivers’ Champion, completing what he believes has been the best season of his career to date.

The Campos Racing driver went into Sunday’s Feature Race 2 tied on points with Freddie Slater, and by finishing second, compared to his rival in eighth, he claimed the title.

Speaking in the paddock afterwards, a delighted Ugochukwu spoke of the importance of winning this championship.

“I'm feeling really good, for sure,” said Ugochukwu. “This was the main goal at the start of the year, to get the championship.

“I think after quali we knew we did our job, we did the main task, and today, and yesterday, it was just about execution and getting the points and bringing it home.

“There was a little bit of pressure which is pretty normal. This last weekend was definitely the most important one of the championship, with two Features.

Ugochukwu kept things calm and controlled out on track on his way to the title in Madrid

“So, quali was pressure to get the job done. I thought I performed with the pressure, I had the right risk versus reward and didn't make any mistakes. Ultimately today, we benefited off the good quali.

“Today I knew what I had to do to win the championship. So, it was in my hands to keep it clean, keep the cars behind at bay, and just bring it home to the line.”

Thoughts of a Champion - Ugo Ugochukwu

FEATURE RACE 2: Taponen wins as Ugochukwu seals 2026 Drivers' title

This result represented a massive turnaround for Ugochukwu as he went into Sunday’s Feature Race in Monza starting at the back of the field, while Slater went from pole.

But with his rival not finishing and him making a comeback to the points, he set himself up for a title showdown in Madrid.

Speaking about his mentality through it all, Ugochukwu said: “I think coming into this weekend, we were quite fortunate to be able to come in 15 points behind.

Ugochukwu is Campos Racing's first FIA Formula 3 Drivers' Champion

“We used that to our advantage. 15 points is still a decent gap, but I knew that was enough to put a bit of pressure on our rivals, and ultimately, we managed to perfect this last weekend, execute it well, and that's what gave us the championship.”

Reflecting more on his season long battle with Slater, Ugochukwu says it was one he enjoyed.

“It was a great battle throughout the year and we really enjoyed it,” he said. “I think beginning of the year, we knew from testing and Round 1 that it might be us two at the end that we would be battling for the championship.

“But to come down like that, to the wire, with equal points in the last race was pretty crazy. So just obviously really happy to get it done and to clinch the title and to come out on top.”

Looking back on the year, Ugochukwu started 2026 winning the Formula Regional Oceania Championship in New Zealand ahead of Slater.

Ugochukwu achieved the goal he set out to at the beginning of the season

The 19-year-old ranks this season as the best of his career to date.

“I think this year is probably one of my top ones of my racing journey, my racing career, 2026 as a whole,” added Ugochukwu.

“Really happy that I've been able to show what I can do. Two titles this year this being my second, and for sure this is the one I really, really wanted to get done.

For sure this is a great step for my career, really important, and it's a good step for what's to come.”

title: Thoughts of a Champion - Ugo Ugochukwu
excerpt:
FIA Formula 3: Welcome, everyone, to the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Champions Press Conference. Many congratulations to our FIA Formula 3 Champion, driving for Campos Racing, Ugo Ugochukwu. Ugo, congratulations. You were locked in a tight battle with Freddie Slater all season. What was your mindset coming here to Madrid with such a close championship battle?

Ugo Ugochukwu: For sure, I was not expecting to come into the final race equal on points, but it made it very exciting. I think we did a good job all weekend. We put ourselves in a good position after qualifying and in the races, so today was just about executing and doing our job properly. P2 was not a bad result. I was just trying to manage my tyres. We knew that was what I needed to win the championship, so it was just about getting it home.

FIA Formula 3: Two victories and seven podiums. You have had a lot of great moments, but is there one moment in the season that stands out for you?

Ugochukwu: I think there are a few. For sure, round one in Melbourne was super special. That was my first win in Formula 3 and it gave me a lot of confidence to continue pushing throughout the season, knowing that we were in the championship fight. Monza was also important, coming back to score a few points. We were fortunate to come into this weekend only 15 points behind, and that really allowed us to apply pressure, attack and ultimately take the championship.

FIA Formula 3: You came back for a second season after a tough rookie year. How much have you learned and matured since stepping into the Formula 3 paddock, and how proud are you of the level of performance you have shown this year?

Ugochukwu: I am super happy. Overall, I think I have improved and evolved as a driver. That is also my goal for the following years, to keep performing better and better. This title is a testament to that, so I am really happy with the work we have put in with the team. I am super happy for them as well, clinching the Teams’ Championship yesterday, and today we got the job done to seal both. It has been pretty much a perfect season for us.

FIA Formula 3: You led the Drivers’ Championship for much of the season, but was there any point when you doubted your title hopes?

Ugochukwu: I would not say I doubted, but there were definitely some points when it looked like we had lost the advantage and needed to come back a little bit. I always kept the faith that I would be able to do it. I had a lot of confidence coming into this weekend, despite being 15 points behind, and I knew it was still possible. We executed everything well, and that allowed us to get the job done.

FIA Formula 3: You are Campos Racing’s first FIA Formula 3 Champion. What does that mean to you, and how key have they been to your success this season?

Ugochukwu: It is super special. The whole team is very happy with this. Our goal at the beginning of the year was to fight for the championship, and that is what we have done. We managed to come out on top, so I cannot thank each and every one of them enough for all their hard work. We have worked well together since before the season started, and I think that really paid off. Starting the championship well is always important, and we finished the season well this weekend too. I am really happy to clinch this first title for Campos.

FIA Formula 3: What is next for the FIA Formula 3 Champion?

Ugochukwu: We will see. Formula 2 is, of course, the next logical step up the ladder towards everyone’s dream of Formula 1. For now, I am just enjoying this title and this championship. The whole of 2026 has been very good for me, winning two championships, and we will see what 2027 brings.
